description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Unintentional weight loss history structure
points: Confirm the loss is genuinely unintentional and quantify amount and timeframe (>5% body weight over 6-12 months is a widely used threshold for concern).
A full systems review is essential — GI, endocrine, psychiatric, and malignancy causes can all present this way.
Night sweats, fevers, and lymphadenopathy point toward malignancy or chronic infection.

modules.title: Weight loss red flags
points: Unintentional weight loss with a palpable mass or lymphadenopathy should be treated as malignancy-suspicious until investigated.
Combine with age-appropriate cancer screening history.

Q000020.why_ask: Loss of appetite alongside weight loss helps distinguish reduced intake from increased losses/metabolic demand.
listen_for: True anorexia vs early satiety vs avoiding food due to pain
Q000020.think: Early satiety with weight loss raises concern for a gastric outlet or infiltrative process.

Q000018.why_ask: Night sweats and fevers alongside weight loss are a classic 'B symptoms' pattern.
Q000018.think: This combination raises lymphoma and chronic infection (e.g. TB) on the differential.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: B-symptoms pattern
points: Consider lymphoma and chronic infection alongside GI malignancy.
Examine specifically for lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly.
